audit.why: 50.69% over 1239 games. Annie holds level 1 and 4-6 on stun-Tibbers threshold; Talon's window is his first lethality item.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] gave level 6 to Talon and whys[5] gave first item to Annie — both are the opposite of win[] and the packet chart.
audit.why: Shadow Assault is 100s at rank 1 and pays off in melee, so 6 is not his swing; the swing is his first lethality item, which win[5] already records as Talon.
audit.corrected: whys[4] and whys[5] flipped to match the chart, with Shadow Assault's real cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Assassin's Path was never described mechanically, and Rake carried no cooldown.
audit.why: Assassin's Path costs 0 mana and has no meaningful cooldown of its own — it is the terrain that goes on a long cooldown after use, at 725 range. Annie has no dash and Molten Shield's speed burst is not one, so a Talon who vaults the wall behind you has cut the retreat outright: Flash is for the wall, not for the damage. Rake is 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s and its return pass carries the bonus damage and the slow.

edits.before: Luden's/Stormsurge spike: the stun-burst math kills through Doran's defenses. Stock, walk forward, win.
edits.after: His lethality item lands first: Talon opens from a wall and finishes before your stun ever comes out.

edits.before: - Talon Rake: matchup-defining — The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E Molten Shield like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Assassin's Path has no cooldown of its own — only the wall he used goes down — so he vaults your retreat and you have no dash. Hold Flash for the wall, not the damage. - Rake is 9s at rank 1; its return is most of his damage. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.

edits.before: The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Rake's return line is most of his lane damage and it is 9s at rank 1 — stand off the return, then step in on the empty window.

edits.before: Carry through the one button — Flash-Tibbers on two is a won fight; your whole game is engineering the radius.
edits.after: Carry by ending it before he re-enters: stun the reveal, Tibbers the landing, and never retreat through a wall he can vault.

edits.before: If Talon opens the score, reset expectations and respect Rake doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with Q refunds and stay relevant through stocked-stun threat.
edits.after: If Talon opens the score, stop walking home past walls — his vault beats your retreat. Farm with Q refunds near tower, hold the glow for the dive, and let Tibbers land on his arrival.

edits.before: Level 6 favors Talon because Shadow Assault lets him vanish and reposition around your stun mid-fight
edits.after: Level 6 favors you because Tibbers and a banked stun beat a 100-second Shadow Assault he has to land in melee

edits.before: First item favors you as your burst punishes his stealth reveal before he can finish his combo
edits.after: First item favors Talon as lethality plus a wall vault opens the fight before your stun ever fires

edits.before: From level 4 you take control again because your Passive stun plus Tibbers is a clean kill threshold on his low base HP before his damage output catches up, though he claws it back exactly at 6 since Shadow Assault lets him vanish mid-fight and reposition around your stun, making that his best engage window.
edits.after: From level 4 you take control because your Passive stun plus Tibbers is a clean kill threshold on his low base HP, and level 6 stays yours: Shadow Assault is 100 seconds at rank 1 and only pays off in melee, so it is his escape more than his opener — the real swing arrives with his first lethality item.

edits.before: Ward the brush he roams through to deny his flank timing
edits.after: Ward the walls he vaults — Assassin's Path cuts your retreat
